D013_m001.question:
"It’s been pretty rough, honestly, since about September, when I first got to college. I just... I can't seem to get anything right. Even walking to class feels like I'm dragging weights, and sometimes my roommate asks me if I'm okay because I just stare blankly. I find myself crying a lot, for no real reason, just out of the blue.

The worst part is this feeling that everything bad that happens is my fault. Last week, one of my professors got sick, and my mind immediately went to some stupid mistake I made in class, like I somehow caused it. It sounds crazy, I know. I even started looking up ways to... you know, just end it all, because I feel like such a burden. I didn’t go through with it, but the thoughts are always there, and they’re getting harder to ignore. I used to be so excited for university, now I can barely motivate myself to get out of bed."
D013_m001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m002.question:
"It's been... I don't know, about five months now, that things have just felt wrong. I can't really pinpoint when it started, but I just feel this heaviness. Sometimes I just start crying for no reason, like a faucet I can't turn off, even when I'm just trying to work. Everything feels like it's in slow motion. My code, my movements, even just walking to the kitchen for a glass of water—it all feels like wading through thick mud.

And the guilt, doctor, it’s crippling. I keep thinking about how that bug slipped through in the last release, and it’s like it’s my fault the whole company is going to fail, even though I know logically it’s not. It feels so real, this burden. Lately, I've been thinking... quite a bit... about just ending it. I've even started picturing how, like, when I'm alone in my apartment after a bad day, or late at night when no one else is awake. I just can’t seem to function like I used to."
D013_m002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m003.question:
"Doctor, thanks for seeing me. Honestly, I’m not sure where to start. It’s been about five months now, maybe more, that I've just felt... heavy. Like there's a constant grey cloud hanging over everything. Getting out of bed feels like I'm trying to lift a truck. Driving, which used to be second nature, now it's like my hands are moving through treacle. Folks beep at me and I just can't seem to get going.

And the guilt, doc, it’s crushing. My ex-wife, her leaving, all the terrible things that have happened in the city... I somehow feel like it’s all my fault. I know it sounds crazy, but it just gnaws at me. The worst part is these flashes I get when I’m driving over a bridge, or when a bus is coming the other way. This sudden, overwhelming urge to just... swerve or jump. No plan, just this terrifying impulse that scares the hell out of me. It's gotten so bad I can barely work; I just can't focus on anything."

A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m030.question: "It's been about six months now, maybe a bit longer, that I've just felt… off. Things I used to enjoy, like going to the local football matches or even just tinkering with the car on a Sunday, they just don't spark anything anymore. I barely even pick up a newspaper. My wife, she notices it too. She says I’m moving slower, like I’m dragging myself through the day. Sometimes even simple things, like getting up to grab a coffee, feel like I'm slogging through mud. My memory isn't what it used to be either; I'm constantly forgetting where I've put my keys or even what stop I'm supposed to be at next – which is a real problem when you're driving a bus full of people. I'm just so tired all the time, even after a full night's sleep. It's not just a physical tiredness, it’s like my whole being is drained. It’s hard to keep up with my routes, let alone anything else at home."
D013_m030.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D013_m031.question: Honestly, Doc, I'm just… flat. It's been like this for about seven months now. Everything feels muted, you know? Like I'm watching my life on a screen instead of living it. I used to thrive on seeing my clients hit their goals, but now when someone tells me they PR'd, it's just… whatever. I don't get that buzz anymore. Training feels like a chore, and sometimes I just can't bring myself to even get out of bed. I’ve dropped a good fifteen pounds without even trying – my clothes are hanging off me. It's hard to explain, but the energy just isn't there. It's really affecting my work and, well, everything.
D013_m031.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m032.question: It’s been pretty rough, honestly. These past seven months, it’s like a piece of me just hollowed out. There’s this constant emptiness inside, like I’m going through the motions but not really feeling anything. I used to be so social, always out with friends, but now... I just can't be bothered. I skip out on dorm gatherings, avoid group study sessions. It’s too much effort to pretend I’m fine. And my appetite has gone through the roof; I'm eating constantly, but it doesn't even make me feel any better. Getting out of bed is a Herculean task most days. Classes feel impossible to focus on, and even simple things like laundry or grabbing groceries feel like monumental efforts. It’s really impacting my grades, and I just don't have the energy to care like I used to.
D013_m032.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m033.question:
"It's been about seven months now that I've just felt… heavy. Not physically, though I have put on a good bit of weight lately – probably five, maybe six pounds a month without even trying. More like a pervasive grey cloud. Even the smallest things, like grading papers or figuring out a new lesson plan, feel like scaling a mountain. My brain just quits on me, like a car sputtering out of gas after a few minutes of trying to focus. It's really hard to get through the school day.

The toughest part is the feeling of apathy. You know, I used to love seeing a student finally 'get' a difficult math concept. There'd be that little spark, that sense of accomplishment. Now? It just registers as another task completed. It's like I’m watching my own life from a distance. I drag myself through the motions, but the enjoyment, the satisfaction, it’s all gone. And frankly, it's starting to affect my work, my ability to connect with the students."
D013_m033.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m034.question:
"To be honest, Doc, I'm just… tired. Bone-tired, not sleeping-enough tired, but deep in my core tired. It’s been building for about seven months now. I just don't have the stomach for anything anymore. My job, you know, it's never been rainbows and sunshine, but I used to find a grim satisfaction in clearing up messes, making things right again. Now? I just stare at the bloodstains and feel… nothing. Even my old hobby, fixing up classic radios, the dust is just collecting on them. I can't bring myself to even pick up a screwdriver.

And the crying, that’s new. Completely out of nowhere, just tears streaming down my face for no good reason. I've also dropped a good twenty pounds without even trying. My clothes are all loose. I guess I just don't eat much anymore. This whole thing has just made it impossible to get through the day; I feel like I'm just going through the motions."
D013_m034.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m035.question:
"It's been about seven months now. Everything just feels… flat. I used to love the market buzz, prepping the cuts, the banter with customers. Now, it's just another day. I go through the motions, but the joy – it's gone. Even after my wife passed, I found solace in my work, but lately, it’s like a thick fog has settled in my head.

I’m eating more, too. Not enjoying it, mind you, just… more. Like I’m trying to fill a hole, but it never really works. And the tiredness, doc, it's something else. My body just feels heavy all the time. Lifting some of the bigger sides of meat, which used to be nothing, now feels like a monumental effort. By the end of the day, I'm absolutely spent, even if I haven't done much. I just don't have the fight in me anymore."
D013_m035.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m036.question: "It's been about three weeks now, maybe a bit more, since I started feeling… empty. Not sad, exactly, just… hollow. Like there’s nothing inside. I’ve barely been eating, and the weight's just melted off me, probably like ten pounds without even trying. My husband’s noticed too, keeps asking if I’m okay, but I just… can’t. Everything feels so slow. Getting dressed in the morning is like moving through mud, and even walking to my car feels like a monumental effort. At work, with the kids, I feel like I'm not doing enough. I know it’s irrational, but I can't shake this feeling that if I'd just done something differently, maybe that last placement wouldn't have gone downhill. It’s like it’s all my fault, every bad thing that happens. I can barely get through the day, let alone focus on anything else."
D013_m036.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D013_m037.question:
"It's been... oh, about three weeks now, maybe a bit more, since I've really felt like myself. There's just this heavy cloud hanging over me, this persistent ache in my chest that just won't lift. It's not just sadness, it's... deeper, more pervasive. Everything feels like wading through thick mud. And my appetite, it's gone through the roof. I'm eating constantly, but it doesn't even make me feel better, just more... full, I guess.

My husband and the teachers keep asking if I'm alright, but honestly, it's hard to get the words out. I find myself just staring, trying to formulate a sentence, and even then, it comes out slow, garbled almost. It’s like my brain just can’t keep up.

And the guilt... that's probably the worst part. I keep thinking about little Jimmy, who fell on the playground last month. It wasn't my fault, the teachers were right there, but I can't shake the feeling that if I'd just been a second quicker, if I'd done something differently, it wouldn't have happened. It's ridiculous, I know, but it feels so real, so heavy. I just can't seem to function like I used to."
D013_m037.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D013_m038.question: "It's been... well, almost three weeks now, I guess. Everything just feels heavier. I try to get things done for the startup, but it's like wading through treacle. My brain just feels foggy, and even simple decisions take forever. My investors are probably going to pull out, and it's all my fault. I keep replaying every mistake I've made, every wrong turn. I mean, we're on the brink of bankruptcy because of *me*. Things just feel so bleak. I've been eating a lot, I think to try and feel something, anything, which isn't helping because I've put on easily ten pounds this month. Sometimes, I just find myself crying, for no real reason, even when I'm trying to work. It's embarrassing. What am I even doing?"
D013_m038.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D013_m039.question:
"It's just... I feel this heavy cloud over me that just won't lift. It's been like this for about three weeks now, a constant ache in my chest that makes everything feel dull. I used to love my meals, especially after long rehearsals, but lately, food just seems unappealing. I barely eat anything, and I've probably lost weight.

I can't sit still, either. My legs are always twitching, or I'm picking at my cuticles without even realizing it. During practice, I find myself pacing backstage, unable to focus on correcting my technique. It's like my body is buzzing with this frantic energy, but my mind is just... blank, or filled with these terrible thoughts.

And the thoughts... I keep thinking it's all my fault. This pandemic, the studio closing for a bit, even the small injury one of the new apprentices got last month. I know it sounds crazy, but I can't shake the feeling that I'm somehow responsible for all the bad things happening around me. It's exhausting, and I feel like I'm letting everyone down, especially with my dancing."
D013_m039.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D013_m040.question:
"Doc, thanks for seeing me. Honestly, I'm just… empty. It's been about three weeks now. I feel like there's nothing inside, just a hollow space where feelings used to be. My wife, she’s noticed too. Says I’m quiet, and yeah, I guess I am. When she asks me something, it just takes me a while to even string a sentence together. It's like my brain's stuck in mud.

And the weight… I've put on maybe ten pounds in the last month. Nothing fits right anymore. All I can think about are these little mistakes I’ve made, going over them again and again. Like that time I miscalculated wiring on a panel last year – it was fixed, no harm done, but it’s all I can think about, how I messed up. It's making it hard to even get on a roof anymore, and that's my livelihood. I just can't shake it."
D013_m040.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D013_m041.question: "I'm here because… well, things just feel really off. It’s been about three months now, maybe a bit more. I just feel this heavy cloud hanging over me, all the time. It’s not just a bad mood, it’s like a constant dull ache. Nothing really brings me joy anymore. My job, being a logistics coordinator, used to be engaging – I liked the challenge, the problem-solving. Now, it’s just a mountain of tasks I can barely bring myself to tackle. Even my usual Friday night football games with the guys, I just can’t get into them. I try to sleep, I really do. I’ll get my eight hours, but I wake up feeling just as tired, if not more so, than when I went to bed. Like my body’s rested but my mind isn’t. I don't know, it's just exhausting existing. There have been a few times, when it just felt like too much to handle, and I actually... I actually thought about ending it all. I know that sounds extreme, but it just feels like there's no way out sometimes."
D013_m041.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m042.question:
For the past three months, it's just been a fog. I'm 48, working at City Hall, and usually, I’m good at my job, detail-oriented. But now, it’s like I’m moving through molasses. There's this hollowness inside, an emptiness, and even when something good happens, like getting a commendation last month, I just don't feel anything. My wife tries to cheer me up, but I'm just… indifferent.

Sleep isn't helping either. I'm sleeping for twelve, sometimes fourteen hours, and I still wake up feeling utterly drained, wanting to just go back to bed. It’s hard to focus at work; things are piling up. Even worse, these thoughts have started creeping in – not just about wanting things to stop, but actual plans. I’ve found myself thinking about how I could just… end it, detailing it out in my head. It's frightening, and I know I need to do something.
D013_m042.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m043.question: It’s been about three months now, maybe a bit longer, since things started feeling… heavy. I just can't shake this cloud that's been hanging over me. Usually, I'm buzzing with ideas for new designs, but lately, I’ve got nothing. Just the thought of picking up my machine feels like lifting a ton of bricks. My clients deserve my best, but I’ve been cancelling appointments, just too drained to even pretend to be enthusiastic. The worst is the sleep, or lack thereof. I’m out by 10, but then bam, 3 AM and my eyes are wide open, staring at the ceiling, my mind just racing. Then those dark thoughts start creeping in – not that I’d ever *do* anything, but sometimes I just wish I could fast forward, or just not wake up, you know? It's really messing with my work, which is everything to me, and I just don’t know how to get back to being myself.
D013_m043.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m044.question:
It's been about three months now, and honestly, I just feel… flat. Like I'm wading through mud all the time. Getting out of bed for work, even though it's just cleaning the subway, feels like climbing a mountain. I used to enjoy a chat with the other cleaners, or even just seeing the morning rush when my shift ended, but now I mostly keep to myself. I just don't have the energy for small talk. All I want to do is go home and be alone.

Sometimes, late at night, especially when I'm alone in my apartment, these thoughts creep in. Not like I'd actually do anything, but just this constant hum of, "I wish I wasn't here," or "It would be easier if I just didn't wake up." My husband passed a few years ago, and I thought I'd moved past the worst of it, but lately, it feels like it's all back, heavier than ever. Sleep isn't much of an escape either. I keep having these awful, vivid nightmares that wake me up in a cold sweat. It just feels like there's no rest, no escape from this feeling. It’s affecting everything – I can barely focus, and just getting through my shift feels like a monumental task.
D013_m044.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m045.question: "Well, doctor, it's been about three months now. Ever since my wife passed, everything just feels… empty. Not sad, exactly, just hollow, like there's nothing left inside. I used to be so proud of what I built, my career, but now it all seems so trivial. Doesn't matter, doesn't bring any joy. I find myself just wanting to sleep all the time, twelve, fourteen hours sometimes. And even then, I wake up tired. Honestly, sometimes I just think it'd be easier if I wasn't here at all, if I could just… not exist. No plans, mind you, just that thought keeps creeping in. It's like I'm just watching the world go by, but I'm not really in it anymore."
D013_m045.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D013_m046.question: It’s been a rough month, doctor. Ever since my husband passed, I just haven't been myself. Most days, I can barely get out of bed, and there's this heavy cloud that just won't lift. Honestly, there's a part of me that feels like it’s my fault he's gone, like I could have done more. I know it sounds silly, but it just gnaws at me. I've also been eating a lot more than usual, probably trying to fill a void. A few weeks ago, I even started gathering up my pills, just thinking it might be easier to just... not be here anymore. I'm not doing much around the house; everything feels like too much effort these days.
D013_m046.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m047.question: "Thanks for seeing me, Doc. It's… tough admitting I need help. For about a month now, I just feel this heavy cloud over everything. It’s not just feeling sad; it’s like constant despair. Even coming in here, it took everything I had. My wife, Sarah, she's noticed, too. We’ve barely eaten dinner together lately – food just doesn’t appeal, never feels hungry, even when I know I should be. I used to pride myself on being strong, being there for people, but now I just feel… useless. Like I'm failing at everything, at work, at home. What kind of cop can't even get out of his own head? A few weeks ago, it got really bad. I found myself just staring at my service weapon, thinking about... well, ending it. I didn't, obviously, but the thought was there, strong enough to scare me into finally booking this appointment. It's hard to focus at work, and even harder to pretend everything's fine when I'm just going through the motions."
D013_m047.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m048.question:
"Doctor, I just feel… heavy. Not just my body, though I’ve put on about ten pounds in the last month without even trying, but my whole being. It's like a cloud has settled over everything, and I can't shake it. My husband keeps asking what's wrong, but I don't even know how to explain this constant sadness. It's been like this for four weeks now.

And the guilt, it's unbearable. My son's company had some layoffs last week, and even though I have nothing to do with it, I can't help but feel it's all my fault somehow. Like I'm a bad mother, and this is happening because of something I did years ago. It’s irrational, I know, but I can't stop thinking about it.

Honestly, sometimes I just wish I wouldn't wake up. Or that a car would just hit me on my way to work. I don't have a plan or anything, but the thought of just… not being here, it crosses my mind more often than I'd like to admit. It’s just so hard to get out of bed and face the day, let alone focus on spreadsheets at work."
D013_m048.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m049.question: "It's been about a month now, maybe a bit longer, since things started feeling really off. I just can't seem to stop the tears from coming, doc, even when there's no real reason for it. My wife, bless her heart, tries to cheer me up, but it's like a faucet I can't turn off. And the eating... I'm eating constantly, more than I ever have, but it doesn't make me feel any better. If anything, it just adds to how useless I feel. What's the point? I see younger guys at work, full of energy, and I just feel like dead weight. Sometimes, I just wish I wasn't around anymore. I wouldn't do anything, not like that, but the thought just keeps popping into my head. It's getting harder to even get out of bed for work, and I can't be doing that; folks rely on me to keep the building clean."
D013_m049.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D013_m050.question:
"Thanks for seeing me, Doc. It’s been… a rough month, honestly. I just feel profoundly down, like there's a heavy blanket over everything. It’s more than just feeling sad; it’s this constant low hum in the background of my mind.

What’s weird is my appetite has gone through the roof. I've been eating way more than usual, especially late at night, almost like I'm trying to fill a void. And the guilt… it's crushing. Every little thing feels like my fault. If a bug slips into the code at work, I beat myself up for days, thinking I’m a failure and deserve whatever bad happens.

Sometimes, I just wish I wouldn't wake up. Not that I’d ever actually do anything, but the idea of just not existing, of not having to deal with any of this, feels incredibly peaceful. It’s making it hard to focus on my work, which is saying something because I usually love coding."
D013_m050.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
